thread:
maria: Quick triage — after the kernel-selection PR landed we saw a ~6–9% P50 regression on host-side parse+tokenize for short-chat requests. Repro locally on my devbox.

sam: Yep, noticed it in staging too. Spike in CPU sys and more time in http/grpc framing when KV cache hit rate is high.

kai: Uploaded a perf profile to the thread: top stacks look like:
```
60% http2::reader::read_frame
20% tokenizer::tokenize
10% kv_cache::lookup (contended)
```

maria: Hm — the runtime switching to fused kernels shouldn't affect host parsing. My suspicion: the new batching heuristics lead to smaller per-request fragments, increasing chunk boundary overhead.

sam: Agree. After the heuristics change, average fragment size dropped from ~4k bytes -> ~512 bytes for short prompts. That multiplies per-chunk parse/serialize cost.

kai: Two quick ideas: bump min_chunk_bytes to 1500 and enable prefix coalescing; and consider moving tokenization off the http worker thread onto a small dedicated pool.

maria: Can we try an offload prototype? I pushed branch feat/parse-worker with a simple parse task queue: ```git checkout feat/parse-worker``` — it keeps HTTP worker only doing framing and enqueuing.

perf-bot: Bench run started (staging, 50 rps, 1k short prompts, 30s ramp) — will post numbers when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: Also noticed KV cache lookup does a single global LRU with a mutex. When chunk count per request rises, we do more lookups and lock contention skyrockets.

maria: Sharding the LRU sounds promising (8 shards?), or try optimistic reads with atomic pointers. Which is faster to implement?

kai: Sharding is quick. I'll run microbench comparing single-shard vs 8-shard LRU under synthetic chunk-heavy load.

perf-bot: Bench results:
- baseline (prior heuristics): P50 45ms
- with parse_worker + chunk_coalesce + min_chunk_bytes=1500: P50 38ms, CPU sys -12%
- KV sharding reduced average kv.lock_wait_ns by 78% under the same workload.

maria: Nice. Proposed rollout: canary 5% with config overrides: min_chunk_bytes=1500, parse_worker=true, kv_shards=8. Monitor latency_heatmap, rpc_error_rate, kv.lock_wait_ns, parse_worker_queue_len.

sam: I'll open the rollout PR and add the canary gating metrics and an automated revert if P99 regresses >10%.

kai: Follow-up tests: add a unit test for chunk boundary coalescing and a microbench for the sharded LRU. Also add a small integration that simulates high KV-hit short prompts.

maria: Logging note — keep sampled payloads small. If we accidentally log huge prompt payloads in the canary we'll blow up traces.

sam: Thanks — I'll also add an observability dashboard tile showing "parse_worker_queue_len" and a flamegraph link for canary traces.

maria: Great work. After canary succeeds we'll roll to 50% and then full. Closing triage, follow-ups: PRs for parse-worker, kv-shard, rollout config, and dashboard. :thumbsup:
